issues.legal_issue: Receipt of compensation without protest bars an application for a reference challenging the compensation award.
material_facts: The claimants received the compensation awarded for their land after signing an agreement accepting the amount, and they did not protest when they received it.

They later objected to the amount and sought a reference for enhanced compensation, claiming that they had protested orally; the High Court found that claim contradicted by the written agreement and evidence.
issues.conclusion: The reference application was not maintainable because the claimants had received compensation without protest. The Supreme Court found no basis to interfere with the High Court’s decision.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 31(2) and 18(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, a person who receives compensation otherwise than under protest is not entitled to apply for a reference challenging the award. Receipt under protest is a condition precedent to an application under Section 18; the application must also meet the applicable limitation requirements and state the grounds of objection under Section 18(2). The Court relied on no earlier cases.

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_reference_: The proceeding concerns a request to refer a dispute about compensation for acquired land for judicial determination.
predicates.compensation_received_without_protest: The claimant received the awarded compensation without protesting at the time of receipt.
predicates.later_application_to_challenge_award: After receiving the compensation, the claimant applied to challenge the award.

issues.definition: When a claimant in a land-acquisition compensation reference proceeding receives compensation without protest and later applies to challenge the award, the reference application is not maintainable.
